_readme: Both calibration sets for the Menlo Ventures run (COLLECTION.md 4), pre-registered 2026-09-06 BEFORE build-company-base.py ran and before any verdict was written. The stage key is built from external documents -- press for the twelve rows where reputation is most likely to be wrong, and the firm's own DATED announcement posts for the rest. It is deliberately independent of the live site's Milestones field ('2011 - Partnered, Series B'), because that field is the layer under test: it is scored against this key and promoted or demoted before the grind is allowed to use it. Taxonomy: Pre-Seed | Seed | Series A | Growth, where Growth is Series B and everything later.

gate_result.verdict: class 1 for the ROUND LABEL; the YEAR is a close year, not an announcement date

the_one_miss.note: Menlo participated in Warby Parker's $12M Series A of Sept 2011; General Catalyst led the Series B a year later and Menlo did not enter there. The site's own year (2011) contradicts its own round word, which is what makes this a layer defect rather than a judgement call.

gate_result.decomposition: The misses do not share a stage -- they share a DATE. Five rows the layer labelled correctly carry a year one earlier than the press announcement (Dropcam 2011 vs Jun-2012, ConverzAI 2024 vs Feb-2025, Orb 2022 vs Mar-2023, Semgrep 2024 vs Feb-2025, and Netlify, dropped). The field is the year the deal CLOSED, not the year it was announced. So the layer is promoted for the round word and constrained for the date: it may set first_seen and it may not be read as an announcement date, and a year disagreement with press never overrides the round word.
evidence_order_for_entry_stage: 1. web_verified citation naming the round and Menlo's participation (class 1)
2. the site Milestones round word (class 1, promoted here at 33/34) -- with its year read as a close year

3. the firm's own dated announcement post naming the round (class 1) -- but it announces the round being ANNOUNCED, which on this firm's book is often a follow-on, not the entry (eero, H1, Goodfire, Numeric all proved this)
5. model with a named deal (class 3), then stage_prior (class 4)
gate_result.caution_recorded: The firm's own announcement archive scored WORSE than its CMS field for this column, which inverts the Creandum finding. Three of the four apparent CMS misses were the announcement layer being wrong: a Menlo post titled 'Our Series A Investment in X' regularly announces the round Menlo LED, months or years after a quieter first cheque. On this firm the announcement is class 1 for the round it names and is NOT evidence that the round is the entry.
